# Blackout wire format test vectors (spec/FORMAT.md). Generated by an independent Swift/CryptoKit implementation.

kind: kdf

# ---- Shared building blocks (spec/FORMAT.md: "Group codes", "Invites", "Group fingerprint", "Plus Codes",
# "Check-ins", "Reports about others", "Are you safe?", "Places"). Generated by an independent Python implementation.
# Lists are written as `a,b` (needs) or space-separated (indices); a missing field means "none".

# Group code clean-up: normalizeCode(input) == output; isGeneratedCode(output) == generated.
kind: code-normalize
input: k7qf 2m9x pa4t w8rj
output: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
generated: true

kind: code-normalize
input: K7QF2M9XPA4TW8RJ
output: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
generated: true

# Underscore, en dash, and an em dash followed by a no-break space between the groups.
kind: code-normalize
input: k7qf_2m9x–pa4t— w8rj
output: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
generated: true

# Leading and trailing spaces, a tab and line breaks: "  k7qf-2m9x<TAB>pa4t<LF>w8rj <LF>".
kind: code-normalize
input_hex: 20206b3771662d326d397809706134740a7738726a200a
output: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
generated: true

kind: code-normalize
input: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
output: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
generated: true

# A 16-letter custom code made only of code symbols is taken for a generated one.
kind: code-normalize

output: ABCD-EFGH-JKMN-PQRS
generated: true

output: K7QF-2M9X-PA4T-W8RJ
generated: true

output: k7qf-2m9x-pa4t-w8rj

# Name keys (spec/FORMAT.md, "Reports about others"): Vouch.key(name) == key. Names and keys are UTF-8 in hex, because

# ---- Replies and reactions (spec/FORMAT.md, "Replies and reactions"). Made by spec/make-reply-vectors.py, an independent
# Python implementation (standard library only) that first rebuilds `kind: message-key` byte for byte. Each `kind: about`
# is a group message sealed with its own key like that vector (same secret and members, member 1, a fixed dummy
# signature); `plain` is the signature and the body with its padding; `mark` is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 of
# `signed_message`, what a reply to THIS message would name it by. `fifth` is the 5th field as sealed; `reads` is what a
# reader makes of it: `reply` or `reaction` (then `about_id` and `about_mark` are the message it names: here the one in
# `kind: message-key`), `ordinary` (the field is ignored), or `nothing` (type 0x02 whose text is no listed reaction:
# not a reaction and not shown at all). A reader that doesn't know the 5th field reads sender, name, text and the
# photo exactly as sealed.
# A reply. No photo: the 4th field is there and empty.

# ---- Which reactions count (spec/FORMAT.md, "Reactions"). `target` is the message looked at, as `<id>:<mark>`. Each `rN`
# is one checked type 0x02 message in the same group, in the order it arrived: member, ts, its own packet id, its own
# mark, the message it names, and its text in hex (`-` for none: it takes the reaction back). `counts` is what is shown
# under the target: text in hex = how many members, in the order of the spec's list; `-` if nothing is shown.
# One per member: the latest ts counts, whatever order they arrive in.

# ---- Journey notes in receipts (spec/FORMAT.md, "Journey notes"). `text` is a receipt's text. `ids` is what a reader that
# doesn't know notes takes from it (the rule of "Delivery receipts"); `entries` what a reader that knows them takes:
# the same ids, each as `id/hops/link` when the token right after it is a note (`?`: a letter this version doesn't
# know, "another link").
# Two ids, each with its note.
kind: receipt-notes
text: 0123456789abcdef h3i 89abcdef01234567 h1b
ids: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567
entries: 0123456789abcdef/3/i 89abcdef01234567/1/b

# Ids with and without a note.
kind: receipt-notes
text: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567 h16r fedcba9876543210
ids: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567 fedcba9876543210
entries: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567/16/r fedcba9876543210

# No notes: a receipt as before.
kind: receipt-notes
text: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567
ids: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567
entries: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567

# A letter this version doesn't know: another link. 0 hops and a leading zero are read.
kind: receipt-notes
text: 0123456789abcdef h2z 89abcdef01234567 h0p fedcba9876543210 h07w
ids: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567 fedcba9876543210
entries: 0123456789abcdef/2/? 89abcdef01234567/0/p fedcba9876543210/7/w

# More than 16 hops, three digits, no digits, no letter, a capital letter: no note.

ids: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567 fedcba9876543210 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567
entries: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567 fedcba9876543210 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567

# Only the token right after an id counts: not a second note, not one after something else, not one at the start.
kind: receipt-notes

ids: 0123456789abcdef 89abcdef01234567 fedcba9876543210
entries: 0123456789abcdef/2/b 89abcdef01234567 fedcba9876543210

# ---- What a reader's phone writes (spec/FORMAT.md, "Journey notes"): `ttl` is the ttl of the first copy of the message
# as it arrived, `link` how it arrived; `note` is the token for the receipt. A ttl above 16 counts as 16.
kind: journey-note
ttl: 15
link: b
note: h1b

kind: journey-note
ttl: 16
link: w
note: h0w

kind: journey-note
ttl: 13
link: i
note: h3i

kind: journey-note
ttl: 1
link: r
note: h15r

kind: journey-note
ttl: 0
link: p
note: h16p

kind: journey-note
ttl: 40
link: i
note: h0i

kind: journey-note
ttl: 64
link: b
note: h0b

# ---- Disappearing messages (spec/FORMAT.md, "Disappearing messages"). Made by spec/make-reply-vectors.py (argument
# `timer`), the independent Python implementation of the vectors above. `kind: timer-field`: `field` is the 5th field
# of a new key, without its 2-byte length; `reads` is the timer in seconds (0: off), or `ignored`.
# Off.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300000000
reads: 0

# 1 hour.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300000e10
reads: 3600

# 8 hours.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300007080
reads: 28800

# 1 day.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300015180
reads: 86400

# 1 week.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300093a80
reads: 604800

# 1 second reads as the shortest, 5 minutes.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300000001
reads: 300

# 299 seconds: the same.
kind: timer-field
field: 030000012b
reads: 300

# 300 seconds, as written.
kind: timer-field
field: 030000012c
reads: 300

# 301 seconds, as written.
kind: timer-field
field: 030000012d
reads: 301

# A week and a second: off.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300093a81
reads: 0

# The largest number: off.
kind: timer-field
field: 03ffffffff
reads: 0

# 4 bytes: ignored.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300000e
reads: ignored

# 6 bytes: ignored.
kind: timer-field
field: 0300000e1000
reads: ignored

# Another type: ignored.
kind: timer-field
field: 0400000e10
reads: ignored

# A reply's field (17 bytes) in a new key: ignored.
kind: timer-field
field: 01e60800000000000533ac1741ddfdd2c7
reads: ignored

# ---- A signed new key with and without the timer (fixed IV, a fixed dummy signature; `digest` is SHA-256 of the signed
# message). `fourth` is the new key as "New keys" lays it out: a reader that knows only four fields reads exactly it
# from both packets. `timer` is what the 5th field says, `none` without one.
# A new key that carries the timer "1 day" in its 5th field.
kind: timer-rekey
code: test-group-1

# ---- Who sets the timer and how epochs inherit it. A phone takes one new key. `had`: it held an epoch before. `maker`:
# `admin` if the key's maker is an admin of the epoch before it (for a phone that had no epoch: if the key's own admin
# list names its maker), else `member`. `kept`: `write`, or `read` for a key numbered below the current epoch, kept only
# to read with. `field`: the key's timer, or `none`. `before`: the timer of the epoch before (`unknown`: not known).
# `timer`: the group's timer on that phone afterwards.
# A phone that joins learns it from the key that lets it in.
kind: timer-epoch
had: no
maker: admin
kept: write
field: 28800
before: unknown
timer: 28800

# Let in by a key without the field: not known yet.
kind: timer-epoch
had: no
maker: admin
kept: write
field: none
before: unknown
timer: unknown

# Never told a value by someone the key doesn't name as an admin.
kind: timer-epoch
had: no
maker: member
kept: write
field: 3600
before: unknown
timer: unknown

# An admin sets it.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: admin
kept: write
field: 3600
before: 86400
timer: 3600

# An admin's key without the field keeps it.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: admin
kept: write
field: none
before: 86400
timer: 86400

# A member's field is ignored.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: member
kept: write
field: 3600
before: 86400
timer: 86400

# A member can't turn it off either.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: member
kept: write
field: 0
before: 86400
timer: 86400

# Only an admin's explicit zero turns it off.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: admin
kept: write
field: 0
before: 86400
timer: 0

# Not known stays not known through a key that inherits.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: member
kept: write
field: none
before: unknown
timer: unknown

# Not known stays not known through an admin's key without the field.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: admin
kept: write
field: none
before: unknown
timer: unknown

# An admin's key brings it to a phone that didn't know it.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: admin
kept: write
field: 604800
before: unknown
timer: 604800

# A member's key kept only to read with changes nothing.
kind: timer-epoch
had: yes
maker: member
kept: read
field: 300
before: 86400
timer: 86400

# ---- Two admins set different timers at once: keys `a` and `b` have one number, both made by admins of the epoch
# before, whose timer was off. `hash_a`, `hash_b`: SHA-256 of each epoch's outer key; the smaller wins. `order`: the
# order the keys reach a phone; `member` is a member's next key, one number higher, without a say on the timer.
# `timer`: the group's timer on that phone afterwards. In the last one the winner comes after the member's key, so it
# is kept only to read with, and is still its admin's word on the timer.
kind: timer-rival
secret_a: 6161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161
secret_b: 6262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262
hash_a: a62d31af9ca0130a2bb46f06b8443822d5c1e4dce959e02348f4cf34c5a14bb1
hash_b: b53b4042180807a9691e3dc45fb9b4aff07f6bc16ec77b06adb93dff1fda8f8c
timer_a: 86400
timer_b: 3600
wins: a
order: a b
timer: 86400

kind: timer-rival
secret_a: 6161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161
secret_b: 6262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262
hash_a: a62d31af9ca0130a2bb46f06b8443822d5c1e4dce959e02348f4cf34c5a14bb1
hash_b: b53b4042180807a9691e3dc45fb9b4aff07f6bc16ec77b06adb93dff1fda8f8c
timer_a: 86400
timer_b: 3600
wins: a
order: b a
timer: 86400

kind: timer-rival
secret_a: 6161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161
secret_b: 6262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262
hash_a: a62d31af9ca0130a2bb46f06b8443822d5c1e4dce959e02348f4cf34c5a14bb1
hash_b: b53b4042180807a9691e3dc45fb9b4aff07f6bc16ec77b06adb93dff1fda8f8c
timer_a: 86400
timer_b: 3600
wins: a
order: a b member
timer: 86400

kind: timer-rival
secret_a: 6161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161616161
secret_b: 6262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262626262
hash_a: a62d31af9ca0130a2bb46f06b8443822d5c1e4dce959e02348f4cf34c5a14bb1
hash_b: b53b4042180807a9691e3dc45fb9b4aff07f6bc16ec77b06adb93dff1fda8f8c
timer_a: 86400
timer_b: 3600
wins: a
order: b member a
timer: 86400

# ---- A key that arrives late, kept only to read with (numbered below the current epoch): epoch N, after a member's
# key N+1 that is current and inherits the timer. `wins`: the late key is the first of every epoch held at N (the order
# of "Current epoch"). `maker`: `admin` if its maker is an admin of the winning epoch before it (N-1), `not-admin` if
# not (an admin demoted at N-1 or earlier, or a member). `field`: its timer, or `none`. `before`: the timer of the
# epoch N that is current at its number (what N+1 inherits without the late key). `timer`: the group's timer
# afterwards. `lines`: whether it may make the chat's lines ("joined", "made an admin", the timer's line).
# An admin's late key that wins at N: its word on the timer, as if it had come in time.
kind: timer-late
wins: yes
maker: admin
field: 3600
before: 86400
timer: 3600
lines: yes

# The same key without the field: the timer stays.
kind: timer-late
wins: yes
maker: admin
field: none
before: 86400
timer: 86400
lines: yes

# A late key that loses at N sets nothing.
kind: timer-late
wins: no
maker: admin
field: 3600
before: 86400
timer: 86400
lines: no

# A late key whose maker isn't an admin of the winning epoch before it (an admin demoted earlier) sets nothing, and freezes nothing.
kind: timer-late
wins: yes
maker: not-admin
field: 300
before: 86400
timer: 86400
lines: no

# Losing and not an admin: nothing.
kind: timer-late
wins: no
maker: not-admin
field: 300
before: 86400
timer: 86400
lines: no

# An admin's late key that wins can turn it off.
kind: timer-late
wins: yes
maker: admin
field: 0
before: 86400
timer: 0
lines: yes

# ---- When a message goes. `seconds`: the group's timer on this phone (`unknown`: not known); `value_since`: since when
# it has had that value. `arrived`: when the message reached the phone, or, written there, first left it (`none`: not
# handed on yet). `high_risk`: the phone is in high-risk mode. `goes`: `timer`, `high-risk`, or `no`.
# Exactly the timer's length after it arrived: it goes.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 3600
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794003600000
high_risk: no
goes: timer

# A millisecond earlier: it stays.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 3600
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794003599999
high_risk: no
goes: no

# The value came 9 minutes 59 seconds ago: it deletes nothing yet.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 3600
value_since: 1794007200000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794007799999
high_risk: no
goes: no

# 10 minutes: it deletes.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 3600
value_since: 1794007200000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794007800000
high_risk: no
goes: timer

# Off: nothing goes by the timer.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 0
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794720000000
high_risk: no
goes: no

# Not known: the normal rule.
kind: timer-due
seconds: unknown
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794720000000
high_risk: no
goes: no

# Written here and not handed on yet: it never goes by the timer.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 3600
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: none
now: 1794720000000
high_risk: no
goes: no

# High-risk mode is due before a week's timer.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 604800
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794086400001
high_risk: yes
goes: high-risk

# High-risk mode counts a day and more: exactly a day stays.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 604800
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794086400000
high_risk: yes
goes: no

# In high-risk mode a shorter timer is due first.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 3600
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794003600000
high_risk: yes
goes: timer

# Off, in high-risk mode: the day.
kind: timer-due
seconds: 0
value_since: 1793913600000
arrived: 1794000000000
now: 1794086400001
high_risk: yes
goes: high-risk

# ---- Leaving the group (spec/FORMAT.md, "Leaving the group"). Made by spec/make-reply-vectors.py (argument `leave`),
# the independent Python implementation of the vectors above. `kind: leave-field`: `field` is a group message's 5th
# field without its length; `framed` is the empty 4th field and the 5th, each behind its 2-byte length, as they follow
# the text; `reads`: `leave` (the note) or `ordinary` (the field is ignored, the message is read as text).
# The note: type 0x05, form 0x01.
kind: leave-field
field: 0501
framed: 000000020501
reads: leave

# Another form (0x02): an ordinary message, read as text.
kind: leave-field
field: 0502
framed: 000000020502
reads: ordinary

# Form 0x00: the same.
kind: leave-field
field: 0500
framed: 000000020500
reads: ordinary

# One byte: ignored.
kind: leave-field
field: 05
framed: 0000000105
reads: ordinary

# Three bytes: ignored.
kind: leave-field
field: 050100
framed: 00000003050100
reads: ordinary

# Type 0x06 with the same byte: not a note.
kind: leave-field
field: 0601
framed: 000000020601
reads: ordinary

# ---- A note, sealed like `kind: about` (member 1's message number 32, a fixed dummy signature). `shown: line`: an app
# that knows the field shows a line, never a bubble, and keeps no copy; `older` is what an app without it shows: the
# text, as an ordinary message (it reads the 5th field as none).
kind: leave-note
secret: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111
member_0: 1111111111111111
member_1: 2222222222222222
position: 1
number: 32
id: e608000000000020
ts: 1794000400032
wire_ts: 1793999246653
sender: 2222222222222222
name: Bea
text: 👋 I left the group
text_hex: f09f918b2049206c656674207468652067726f7570
fifth: 0501
iv: 545454545454545454545454
signature: 07070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707
plain: 
signed_message: 
cipher: 
reads: leave
shown: line
older: 👋 I left the group

# ---- Which notes count (rule L1). `epoch_N`: an epoch this phone holds, number N, with its member list (comma-separated);
# `read_N: yes`: kept only to read with (the list is whatever its maker wrote); `removes_N`: a removal that took that
# member out (it has a new code). `epoch_N` is the winner of its number (of the epochs with a member list); the highest
# is the current one. `rival_N`: the member list of a rival at N that lost to it (made by a member who isn't an admin):
# only the winner at each number counts. `opened_by`: the epoch whose key opened the note. `checked`: its signature
# checked (`yes`), failed (`no`), or can't be checked yet (`not-yet`). `me`: this phone. `valid`: `valid`, `no`, or
# `not yet` (decided when it checks). Check-in clocks count by the same rule ("If I go quiet", Q1).
# Sealed in the current epoch, which lists the sender.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: valid

# Sealed in epoch 5; the current one is 6; both list the sender.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: valid

# Removed at 6, let in again at 7 with the same key: the note sealed in 5, played back now, does nothing.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222
removes_6: 3333333333333333
epoch_7: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# Left out of 6 by a key, let in again at 7: the same.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222
epoch_7: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# Removed at 6: a removed member's note does nothing.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222
removes_6: 3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# Opened by an epoch kept only to read with.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
read_5: yes
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# Epoch 6 isn't on this phone: nothing shows that it listed the sender.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
epoch_7: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# Its signature can't be checked yet.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: not-yet
valid: not yet

# Its signature fails.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: no
valid: no

# This phone's own note.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 1111111111111111
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# An admin let C in with key 6 while a member's weekly key 6 left C out; the admin's won. That losing rival doesn't matter: C's note counts.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
rival_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222
epoch_7: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 6
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: valid

# The other way round: the winner at 6 leaves C out and a rival that lost lists C. The note does nothing.
kind: leave-valid
epoch_5: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
epoch_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222
rival_6: 1111111111111111,2222222222222222,3333333333333333
opened_by: 5
sender: 3333333333333333
me: 1111111111111111
checked: yes
valid: no

# ---- What a phone does about a valid note (rule L4). `admin`: this phone is an admin of the current epoch and wasn't
# removed. `in_current`: the member is still in the current epoch. `removal_held`: a removal of them is on this phone
# already. `keys`: this phone has the encryption keys of every member who stays. `act`: `remove-now` (the normal
# removal, after 0 to 3 s), `retry-hourly`, or `nothing`.
kind: leave-admin
admin: yes
in_current: yes
removal_held: no
keys: yes
act: remove-now

kind: leave-admin
admin: yes
in_current: yes
removal_held: no
keys: no
act: retry-hourly

kind: leave-admin

# ---- What is shown from the member who left (rule L3). `note_ts`: their note's ts; `sender`, `ts`: a message of the same
# group; `shown`: whether it is shown, alerted, confirmed and counted.
# A minute before the note.
kind: leave-after
leaver: 3333333333333333
note_ts: 1794000500000
sender: 3333333333333333
ts: 1794000499999
shown: yes

# At the note's own time.
kind: leave-after
leaver: 3333333333333333
note_ts: 1794000500000
sender: 3333333333333333
ts: 1794000500000
shown: yes

# A millisecond after the note.
kind: leave-after
leaver: 3333333333333333
note_ts: 1794000500000
sender: 3333333333333333
ts: 1794000500001
shown: no

# Someone else, after the note.
kind: leave-after
leaver: 3333333333333333
note_ts: 1794000500000
sender: 2222222222222222
ts: 1794000500001
shown: yes

# ---- If I go quiet (spec/FORMAT.md, "If I go quiet"). Made by spec/make-reply-vectors.py (argument `quiet`), the
# independent Python implementation of the vectors above. `kind: quiet-field`: `field` is a group message's 5th field
# without its length; `framed` is the empty 4th field and the 5th, each behind its 2-byte length, as they follow the
# text; `reads`: `clock` with its `deadline` (ms since 1970 UTC, signed 64-bit big-endian; 0 stops), or `ordinary`
# (the field is ignored, the message is read as text). `ts`, `valid`: the message's own time, and rule Q2 for it.
# The brief's example: ts 1793807238631, 1 hour.
kind: quiet-field
field: 04000001a1a7753467
framed: 0000000904000001a1a7753467
reads: clock
deadline: 1793810838631
ts: 1793807238631
valid: yes

# Deadline 0: a stop.
kind: quiet-field
field: 040000000000000000
framed: 00000009040000000000000000
reads: clock
deadline: 0
ts: 1793807238631
valid: yes

# 8 bytes: ignored.
kind: quiet-field
field: 04000001a1a77534
framed: 0000000804000001a1a77534
reads: ordinary

# 10 bytes: ignored.
kind: quiet-field
field: 04000001a1a775346700
framed: 0000000a04000001a1a775346700
reads: ordinary

# Type 0x06 with 8 bytes: not a clock.
kind: quiet-field
field: 06000001a1a7753467
framed: 0000000906000001a1a7753467
reads: ordinary

# ---- A clock message, sealed like `kind: about` (member 1's message number 33, a fixed dummy signature), 1 hour 30
# minutes. `shown: card`: an app that knows the field shows a card, alerts and confirms it, and keeps a copy; `older` is
# what an app without it shows: the text, as an ordinary message (it reads the 5th field as none).
kind: quiet-message
secret: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111
member_0: 1111111111111111
member_1: 2222222222222222
position: 1
number: 33
id: e608000000000021
ts: 1794000600033
wire_ts: 1793999322240
sender: 2222222222222222
name: Bea
text: ⏳ Check on me if I don't check in within 1 hour 30 minutes

fifth: 04000001a1b31721a1
deadline: 1794006000033

signature: 07070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707070707
plain: 
signed_message: 
cipher: 
mark: c38dfbdeef09cc91
reads: clock
shown: card

# ---- Rule Q2: which deadlines count for a message dated `ts`. `valid: no`: the field is ignored and the message is an
# ordinary text.
# 4 minutes 59 seconds after.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 1794000299000
valid: no

# 5 minutes after.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 1794000300000
valid: yes

# 24 hours after.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 1794086400000
valid: yes

# 24 hours and 1 ms after.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 1794086400001
valid: no

# Before the message.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 1793999940000
valid: no

# Negative.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: -1
valid: no

# 0: a stop.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 0
valid: yes

# The largest number.
kind: quiet-valid
ts: 1794000000000
deadline: 9223372036854775807
valid: no

# ---- Rule Q3: which clock message of a member counts. `clock_X`: `ts id mark deadline`; `arrival`: the order they
# reached the phone; `counts`: the one that counts, whatever the order: the greatest ts, then the greater packet id
# (16 lowercase hex chars), then the greater mark (the first 8 bytes of the signed digest, hex).
# Three clocks, arriving C, A, B, with ts A < B < C: C counts.
kind: quiet-pick
clock_A: 1794000000000 e608000000000101 00000000000000aa 1794003600000
clock_B: 1794000060000 e608000000000102 00000000000000bb 1794007200000
clock_C: 1794000120000 e608000000000103 00000000000000cc 1794001920000
arrival: C,A,B
counts: C

# A stop newer than a clock: the stop counts, the member has no clock.
kind: quiet-pick
clock_A: 1794000000000 e608000000000101 00000000000000aa 1794003600000
clock_B: 1794000060000 e608000000000102 00000000000000bb 0
arrival: B,A
counts: B

# The same ts: the greater packet id.
kind: quiet-pick
clock_A: 1794000000000 e608000000000201 00000000000000ff 1794003600000
clock_B: 1794000000000 e608000000000202 0000000000000001 1794007200000
arrival: B,A
counts: B

# The same ts and id: the greater mark.
kind: quiet-pick
clock_A: 1794000000000 e608000000000301 1000000000000000 1794003600000
clock_B: 1794000000000 e608000000000301 0fffffffffffffff 1794007200000
arrival: B,A
counts: A

# ---- Rule Q4: what cancels a member's clock dated `clock_ts`. `ts`, `text_hex`, `fifth` (if any): a later group message
# of the same member; `what`: what it is; `cancels`: whether the clock is no longer armed after it. A stop cancels by
# rule Q3 (it is the newer clock message); a check-in by rule Q4.
kind: quiet-cancel

# ---- Rules Q5 to Q7: what a phone does about an armed clock. `learned`: when the phone took it; `now`; `armed`: no
# cancelling check-in or newer clock message reached it. `does`: `at-deadline` (an alert scheduled for the deadline),
# `now` (an alert at once, worded as on time), `late` (at once, with "This phone learned of it late.") or `none`.
# Learned an hour before the deadline.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1793996400000
now: 1793996400000
armed: yes
does: at-deadline

# Learned at the deadline.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1794000000000
now: 1794000000000
armed: yes
does: now

# Held before, the deadline came while the app was away.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1793996400000
now: 1794003600000
armed: yes
does: now

# Learned 11 h 59 min after.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1794043140000
now: 1794043140000
armed: yes
does: late

# Learned 12 h after.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1794043200000
now: 1794043200000
armed: yes
does: late

# Learned 12 h and 1 ms after.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1794043200001
now: 1794043200001
armed: yes
does: none

# Held before, 12 h and 1 ms after.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1793999940000
now: 1794043200001
armed: yes
does: none

# Cancelled.
kind: quiet-late
deadline: 1794000000000
learned: 1794000060000
now: 1794000060000
armed: no
does: none

# ---- Voice notes (spec/FORMAT.md, "Voice notes"). Made by spec/make-reply-vectors.py (argument `voice`), the
# independent Python implementation of the vectors above. `kind: voice-field`: `field` is a group message's 4th field
# without its 2-byte length, type byte `02` first; `text_hex` the message's 3rd field; `bytes` how many follow the type
# byte. `reads: voice`: a reader keeps the note, `packets` long (`ms`, and `seconds` / `label` as shown); `reads: text`:
# the field is ignored as a whole and the message is its text. The packets are made up (`syn` in the script): only
# their lengths and first two bytes matter to the rules, not whether a decoder makes sound of them.
# The shortest: 50 packets of 1 byte, the TOC byte alone (a frame of 0 bytes, as RFC 6716 allows).
kind: voice-field
text_hex: f09f8ea420566f696365206e6f7465
field: 0201080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108010801080108
bytes: 100
reads: voice
packets: 50
ms: 1000
seconds: 1
label: 0:01

# 350 packets of 3 bytes: 7 seconds.
kind: voice-field
text_hex: f09f8ea420566f696365206e6f7465
field: 
bytes: 1400
reads: voice
packets: 350
ms: 7000
seconds: 7
label: 0:07

# 74 packets: 1.48 s, shown as 0:01.

field: 
bytes: 222
reads: voice
packets: 74
ms: 1480
seconds: 1
label: 0:01

# 75 packets: 1.5 s, rounded up to 0:02.

field: 
bytes: 225

packets: 75

# ---- What a writer sends of what its encoder wrote (spec/FORMAT.md, "Voice notes", writers). `fixture` is a field from
# the codec experiment of 2026-11-22: Apple's system Opus encoder, variable bitrate, 8000 bit/s, 48 kHz, ten seconds of
# speech, every packet as it came (501: start-up delay and the final flush). It is in app/src/test/voice and
# ios/BlackoutCore/Tests/voice. `fixture_reads`: as it came, readers ignore it; a writer keeps the first 500 packets,
# which give the field `kept_sha256` (SHA-256 of the field, type byte included), `kept_bytes` after the type byte.
kind: voice-trim
fixture: apple-8k-vbr-48000.voicefield
fixture_sha256: 4841ece5e733abfb4a0e9d053e7f6763f0a3d3910f9155804764e841a9b62257
fixture_bytes: 9701
fixture_packets: 501
fixture_reads: text
kept_packets: 500
kept_bytes: 9686
kept_sha256: 9ddf09edc153c408102a8abcc5dd41a56667439588f6087eca4f76af83bba67e
reads: voice
seconds: 10

# ---- A voice note that answers a message (spec/FORMAT.md, "Voice notes", "Replies"): the 4th field is the note, the
# 5th the reply to the message of `kind: message-key`. Sealed like `kind: about` (member 1's message number 40, a fixed
# dummy signature). `older`: what an app without voice notes shows, the text.
kind: voice-message
secret: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111
member_0: 1111111111111111
member_1: 2222222222222222
position: 1
